title: Ground-Level NO2 Surveillance from Space Across China for High Resolution Using Interpretable Spatiotemporally Weighted Artificial Intelligence.
summary: The models produced 100%-coverage daily 1-km estimates for China in 2019–2020, with out-of-sample/out-of-city R2 0.93/0.71. Analysis found average urban-rural differences of 28%, Spring Festival and National Day declines of 22% and 14%, and slower post-lockdown recovery in surface concentrations than satellite columns. Ground measurements from approximately 1,630 stations were used with out-of-sample and out-of-city cross-validation; the article reports RMSEs and spatial/temporal pattern checks. Estimates are model-derived, and the paper does not establish causal explanations for the observed urban, holiday, or pandemic patterns.
ai_technology: Spatiotemporally weighted extra-trees fill satellite tropospheric NO2 gaps; spatiotemporally weighted deep forest combines satellite columns, ground measurements, reanalysis, and model simulations to estimate daily surface NO2 at 1-km resolution.

source_review.scope: The primary full text reports a daily, full-coverage 1-km surface NO2 dataset for mainland China, generated by filling satellite gaps and estimating ground concentrations with spatiotemporally weighted extra-trees and deep-forest models. Out-of-sample/out-of-city cross-validation R2 was 0.93/0.71 (RMSE 4.89/9.95 μg/m3); the paper reports 28% average urban-rural differences and holiday declines. The first located result-bearing source is the ACS article dated 2022-06-29; catalog checks found related earlier NO2 estimation work but no same dataset or same findings.
